l.i: telligentia Verbi divini lingua Hebraea & Gra-câ conscripti, fundamentum habet, promovendum, benignè & clementer approbaturi fitis. Quod cum de Vobis intellexero, abundè magnum horum studiorum fructum consecutus videbor. Oro autem Filium Dei, Iesum Christum, ut det Vobis diu videre Terram vestram Pace, Concor-dia, Religione, Disciplina florentem, ad Dei gloriam & Ecclesiae bonum.

main_text.l: EN vobis sextam, ex benedictione Divina, Lexici hujus editionem. Felix haec distractio inescavit alios, ut illi quoque huic praedae inbiarent. Eam enim dum paramus, fama ad nos defert, Franekerae idem & eadem excudi formâ. Neque ea vana fuit. Brevi enim pòst, accepto trium foliorum specimine, plena rei fides nobis facta fuit, ut jam ad sufflaminandum illum conatum nihil amplius fuerit consilii. Non jam facti hujus enormitatem, quod facile possem, exaggerabo. Charitati, quam profitemur, repugnat, cum proximi dispendio suum quaerere compendium: Juri & justitiae, alienum sibi, invito & inscio Domino vendicare, falcemque suam in alienam messem mittere. Hactenus

page.notes: The dedication fragment at the top is italic and begins mid-word, so it is kept as a fragment and marked cont="true". The date line "M. DC. VII." is in small capitals. The drop cap "E" is joined to "N" as "EN". Printed "sextam" appears as "fextam", and "distractio" as "diftractio"; both were corrected to the standard spelling. "Hactenus" at the foot is the last word of the page, printed as a catchword. The ornament between the dedication and the title is not text and is omitted. The small "1" at the lower right is read as a page number.
